To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pigs that are parasite-naïve and raised in a specific pathogen-free environment remain highly susceptible to Ascaris infection and (2) pigs that are exposed naturally to Ascaris develop a strong protective immune response and become resistant to re-infection.

pigs raised in a parasite-free herd are susceptible to Ascaris infection and develop a strong pre-hepatic resistance, but pigs raised in a naturally exposed herd are resistant to infection and develop a complete pre-hepatocellular resistance.
parasite naïve growers, finishers or sows have a relatively low level of resistance to Ascaris infection while naturally exposed pigs of all ages are highly resistant.

the age-related resistance of the parasite naïve herd is not sufficient to prevent infection and that the only effective means of controlling A. suum infection in swine is to maintain herds parasite free.
